install.chain_blocked_by_hookspath: **refusing to install**: this repo already has `core.hooksPath=%(value)s` — once git has that, it never looks at `.git/hooks`, so a wrapper written here would never run.
install.chain_blocked_fix: pick one: run `python3 reflect-hooks/install.py --uninstall` to drop the old wiring, then `--chain`; or keep the old wiring (it runs the gates too) and do not use `--chain`.
install.chain_done: chained wrapper installed. undo: python3 reflect-hooks/install.py --uninstall
install.chain_hint: for a ready-made hookup: python3 reflect-hooks/install.py --chain
install.intro: Einfacht does not steal the hook seat — it exposes one entry point that your hook system calls itself:
install.kept_existing: kept the existing %(name)s as %(name)s.einfacht-prev (it runs before Einfacht)
install.legacy_warning: ! this silences .git/hooks/ entirely — other hook tools go silently dead.
install.not_a_repo: '%(path)s' is not a git repo (no .git found)
install.usage_chain: --chain      install chained wrappers in .git/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push}: an existing hook runs first, then Einfacht (no seat-stealing)
install.usage_legacy: --legacy     old install: git config core.hooksPath reflect-hooks (silences every other hook in .git/hooks)
install.usage_no_target: no target repo root ⇒ installs into this repo (where the toolkit lives). Always pass it when installing elsewhere.
install.why_not_hookspath: why not core.hooksPath any more: it is a global override switch — once set, git ignores .git/hooks entirely, so husky / lefthook / pre-commit / hand-written hooks silently die (commits still succeed, no warning).
